english: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ and $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=x^{3}+ax^{2}+bx$ and
If the composite function $f\circ g$ is differentiable at $x=0$, then the value of $(f\circ g)'(0)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $a$ तथा $b$ वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं। माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ तथा $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=x^{3}+ax^{2}+bx$ तथा
द्वारा परिभाषित हैं। यदि संयुक्त फलन $f\circ g$, $x=0$ पर अवकलनीय है, तो $(f\circ g)'(0)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $g$ jumps at $0$ ($g(0^{-})=-1$, $g(0)=1$), so the chain rule does not apply directly; work with one-sided pieces
solution_full: $g$ is not continuous at $0$: $\lim_{x\to0^{-}}g(x)=-1$ while $g(0)=1$. So the chain rule cannot be applied at $0$, and $h=f\circ g$ must be examined from each side.
Since $h(0^{-})=h(0)$, the left derivative is $\lim_{x\to0^{-}}\dfrac{f(x-1)-f(-1)}{x}=f'(-1)=2-2a$. The right derivative is $\lim_{x\to0^{+}}\dfrac{f(4x+1)-f(1)}{x}=4f'(1)=8+8a$.
originality_note: New: the inner function has a jump, yet the composite is made differentiable because the outer cubic takes equal values at the two one-sided limits and its slopes there compensate the different slopes of the inner pieces (way 4: a hidden invariant f(-1) = f(1) hides the jump). Closest known: differentiability of f(g(x)) where g is continuous with a corner. Different because: g is discontinuous, so the chain rule fails and continuity of the composite must be imposed through f(-1) = f(1).
key_step: Split f(g(x)) into f(x-1) and f(4x+1); continuity gives f(-1) = f(1), equal one-sided derivatives give f'(-1) = 4 f'(1).
justification: Routine chain of two conditions (continuity and derivative matching) after noticing that the chain rule cannot be used at the jump; light algebra. Comparable to 2024-P1-Q1 (L2); the discontinuous inner function stops it from being L1.

concept_use.Continuity and Differentiability of comp: f o g is studied as f(x-1) and f(4x+1) because g jumps at 0; the composite is continuous only if f(-1) = f(1).
concept_use.Continuity and Differentiability of func: Equality of the one-sided derivatives f'(-1) and 4 f'(1) of the composite at 0 gives a = -3/5 and the value 16/5.

stem_review: Read as a student: a, b, f and g (domains, codomains, both pieces of g) are defined; 'composite function f o g differentiable at x = 0' has one reading. Checked with sympy (a = -3/5, b = -1) and numerically that both one-sided difference quotients tend to 3.2. Answer 3.20, a positive decimal. Changed: No change.
